premises: High configurational entropy in spinel oxides reduces Gibbs free energy and stabilizes the oxide against deactivation by water.
High-entropy oxide (HEO) spinels exhibit low H2O adsorption energy and strong hydrothermal stability, enabling long-term water-resistant oxidation.
Porous HEO nanostructures can physically confine and stabilize supported metal nanoparticles against sintering up to 850–1000 °C.
A conformal HEO coating can be deposited as a thin (<10 nm), nanoporous layer that provides additional oxygen activation sites.
The HEO coating moderates adsorption energies of H2O and NO, thereby improving poisoning resistance.
